judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 351. Dangerous excessive speeding means driving at least 50 miles per hour over the limit or at least 100 miles per hour while threatening people or property; first penalties reach 30 days and $500, then 90 days and $1,000. A second conviction within five years suspends driving for 180 days to one year, and anyone cited for more than 50 miles per hour over must attend a hearing. The Florida House passed it 75-38, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for the House version of House Bill 875. It orders updated teaching standards, one core teacher-training curriculum, a skills-based certification route called Coaching for Educator Readiness and Teaching, and common mentor rules. The House passed it 84-27; the final law also names two required courses, creates the Florida Center for Teaching Excellence at Miami-Dade College, and keeps the general-knowledge exam.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against the House version of House Bill 875. judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 903. Prisoners must finish prison appeals before suing, cannot claim only mental harm without physical injury or a listed sexual act, and have one year for poor-person petitions and injury suits. Discipline challenges create account liens for court costs; 10-20-Life gun terms run one after another, and another constitutional execution method may replace lethal injection if its chemicals become unavailable or impractical. The Florida House passed it 83-33, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 1219. The CHOICE Act lets non-health workers earning over twice their county's average wage sign deals lasting up to four years that pay them to avoid rivals or bar rival work, and says these are not trade restraints. Courts must temporarily stop similar work unless strong evidence shows it differs or the employer stopped agreed pay and benefits. The Florida Senate passed it 28-9, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 6025. It repeals the automatic ban on selling, displaying, or publicly carrying guns and ammunition during a local emergency caused by violence or disorder. The repealed section also said it did not authorize taking lawfully owned guns. The Florida House passed it 86-28, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 56. Purposely releasing material into Florida's air to change weather, climate, temperature, or sunlight becomes a third-degree felony, with up to five years and $100,000, or up to $5,000 for aircraft workers. Public airports must report equipped aircraft, environmental officials must investigate reports, and Florida ends its weather-modification licenses and research power. The Florida Senate passed it 28-9, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 492. Wetland banks release credits on a fixed schedule: 30 percent after land protection and funding, 30 percent after construction, 20 percent at an interim target, and 20 percent at final success, or all credits for preservation-only banks. Created-wetland credits may come early, and applicants get one use of credits outside the service area when none are available inside it. The Florida House passed it 87-26, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for the Senate version of Senate Bill 1080. It standardizes zoning details, deadlines, and fee refunds; bars hearing limits that cause delay; speeds building on farmland surrounded by development; and limits steep increases in impact fees, which fund public services. The Senate passed it 26-8; the final law also withdraws plan changes unfinished within 180 days after a second hearing and allows code fees for permit work.
